subject: Brisingid
topic: This sea star holds its arms up into the water like a feathery net.
script:
This sea star holds its arms up into the water like a feathery net.
It's a brisingid sea star.
Instead of crawling after food, it catches it straight from the water.
Its long, spiny arms snag tiny animals drifting past in the current.
But look closely. It has a sneaky neighbor.
A scale worm lives right next to it.
Scientists think worms like this stay close so they can steal the food the sea star catches.
It's called kleptoparasitism, which simply means being a parasite by theft.
This pair was filmed in twenty twenty-six, off American Samoa.
Would you put up with a roommate who steals your food?
